Subject: Question on product ownership and feedback license in MSA

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and attached the redline (NovaPro_MSA_Redline_v2.docx). Two quick areas we need clarity on before procurement can proceed:

1) Output ownership: the draft says Redwood grants a "license" to use outputs. NovaPro's position is that where we pay for a productized model feature and embed it into our product, we should have assignment of the specific output templates for our proprietary features (not a blanket ownership of Redwood models). Can you confirm whether a narrow assignment is something Redwood will consider and under what limits?

2) Feedback / training license: the redline requests a broad perpetual license to use any submitted data for model training. We need either explicit opt-in or clear carveouts for customer confidential data and PII. Please advise what standard language you can accept that preserves our ability to opt out for certain data classes.

Also: procurement asked for evidence of how customer data is segregated (high level) and any SOC2 scope docs. I've attached the redline. Can we schedule a short legal sync this week?

Attachments: NovaPro_MSA_Redline_v2.docx (docx)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: Question on product ownership and feedback license in MSA

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear notes and for sending the redline. Quick answers and a suggested path forward below.

On output ownership: Redwood's default is to grant customers a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use outputs produced for them. Full assignment of our underlying model or broad assignment of all outputs is not something we do by default. That said, we can agree to a narrow assignment limited to: (a) "Delivered Product Instances" where NovaPro pays an additional productization fee and (b) instances that are described in the Order Form (i.e., specific model artifacts or fine-tuned artifacts created exclusively for NovaPro).

Proposed short clause (suggestion):
"For any Deliverable Product Instances specifically identified in an Order Form and paid for under a Productization Fee, Redwood will assign to Customer all right, title and interest in the output artifacts generated solely for Customer use, subject to Redwood's pre-existing intellectual property and third-party rights. For avoidance of doubt, Customer does not receive rights to Redwood's underlying model weights, training data, or general-purpose model improvements."

On feedback / training license: we require explicit opt-in for training on customer-provided data. Our standard approach is: customer may opt in (or opt out) per Order Form; Redwood will not use data categorized as Confidential or PII for model training without prior written consent. For procurement evidence, I'm attaching an anonymized data map we share with procurement teams (evidence_customer_data_map.csv) that outlines where data flows and retention controls.

If that trade (narrow assignment + opt-in training) sounds workable, we can redline the document to include the suggested clause and a checkbox in the Order Form for training opt-in. If NovaPro needs assignment for downstream sublicensing/productization, we'll need to route that to pricing (there may be a Productization Fee).

Proposed next step: legal sync Wed 6/19 10:00-10:30 PT — will that work for your team?

Attachments referenced: evidence_customer_data_map.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Rachel Kim

Internal — quick thoughts before we send a redline back:

Thanks Rachel — this framing looks good. A couple of operational points to bring into the redline and procurement playbook:

- We should be explicit about what counts as a "Delivered Product Instance" (e.g., fine-tuned checkpoint, exported prompt templates, packaged model artifact). Avoid vague language that Procurement will read as "all outputs".
- For any assignment, require a Productization Fee and a limited warranty/acceptance period. That keeps legal/procurement comfortable.
- For training opt-in, add a checkbox in the Order Form and an appendix that lists excluded data classes (PII, regulated data, customer-specified confidential categories). NovaPro can request evidence (SOC2 report, data flow map) — we should be prepared to provide SOC2 summary and the evidence CSV Rachel mentioned.

I'll draft a redline of the specific clause that includes a short definition section and the Productization Fee reference. Rachel — can you take the lead on proposing language back to NovaPro and book the 6/19 sync? I'll loop Pricing if they ask for fee numbers.

Emily — thanks again for the redline and patience while we scoped options. Below is a concise summary of where Redwood can land and what we will include in a formal redline document (attached).

Summary of proposed path: 
1) Narrow assignment carveout: Redwood will agree to assign rights to "Delivered Product Instances" only when (a) the instance is specifically identified in the Order Form, and (b) a Productization Fee is paid. Assignment will be limited to the generated artifacts described in the Order Form and will expressly exclude Redwood's model weights, training corpus, and any improvements made to Redwood's service generally.

2) Training / feedback: Redwood will not use Customer Data for model training unless the Order Form includes an explicit "Training Opt-In" checkbox. Data marked Confidential or containing PII will be excluded from training unless Customer provides written consent.

3) Evidence & security docs: Redwood will provide a SOC2 summary and the data flow/segregation CSV (evidence_customer_data_map.csv). For procurement, we can also provide a short runbook describing retention windows and deletion hooks.

4) Next steps: I have attached a short redline summary (we also updated NovaPro_MSA_Redline_v2.docx) with the suggested clause and an Order Form checkbox. Proposed legal sync: Thu 2024-06-20 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET — please confirm. If Pricing is needed for the Productization Fee, I'll invite them.
